title: How Does Face Unlock Know It's Really You?
description: How does face unlock recognise you in half a second, even in the dark? Your phone never stores a photo of your face — instead it converts your face into a list of about 128 abstract numbers using a neural network trained on millions of faces. This video explains the two phases (setup and every unlock), how phones with a depth sensor fire invisible light to build a 3D map that a flat photo cannot fake, and why your face data never leaves your device. Clear for complete beginners.
pinned_comment: Can a good photo of you unlock your phone — or does it depend on which phone you have?

terms.plain: a program trained on millions of faces

scenes.say: Your phone unlocked in the dark before your hand even steadied. How does it know this face is yours and not a stranger's?

visual.caption: *Half a second.* How does it really know?

scenes.say: Here's the trick — it never stores a photo. It stores about 128 abstract numbers, none of them with human-readable names.

visual.sub: abstract values your face maps to

scenes.say: Think of it like a mark-sheet for your face — a unique combination no one else shares. <laugh>
During setup, a neural network — a program trained on millions of faces — builds that number list and saves it in a locked chip: a separate processor no app can touch.
Each unlock, the same program reads your fresh face, makes a new list, and measures how far it sits from your saved one. Close enough? Open.
That comparison alone takes under 100 milliseconds. The whole unlock? About 0.3 seconds total.
Phones with a depth sensor fire invisible light at your face. Close one eye — world goes flat, like a photo. No depth to fake.
Grow a beard? Numbers update when the phone is confident enough it's you. Identical twins? Their numbers sit very close. Known weak spot.

items.text: Beard or glasses: updates when confident
Dark room: depth sensor works fine

scenes.say: And those numbers never leave your phone — invisible to every app.
Depth sensor, neural network, number check — all done as you glance at a screen.
Your phone doesn't recognise your face. It recognises your numbers. Stay curious. Thoma out!

visual.text: Your phone reads *your numbers*, not your face
